title: Why a bar beats a spot

scenes.tts: Hubel and Wiesel recorded from single cells in the visual cortex of anaesthetized cats. They projected spots of light onto a screen. Spots drive the retina well. In the cortex, spots often did little. Bars at the right orientation drove cells hard. Why would a bar win?
scenes.visual: Screen with a spot, then a bar; spike ticks for one cortical cell stay sparse for the spot and fill in for the bar.
scenes.narration: Hubel and Wiesel recorded from single cells in the visual cortex of anaesthetized cats. They projected spots of light onto a screen. Spots drive the retina well. In the cortex, spots often did little. Bars at the right orientation drove cells hard. Why would a bar win?

scenes.tts: A receptive field is the region of the visual field where a stimulus changes a neuron's firing. Hubel and Wiesel recorded with an electrode outside the cell. They mapped each field with spots, slits and bars. Moving a stimulus and counting spikes shows where the field lies.
scenes.visual: Electrode beside a cell; a light spot moves across the screen; where spikes change, a dashed field outline is drawn.
scenes.narration: A receptive field is the region of the visual field where a stimulus changes a neuron's firing. Hubel and Wiesel recorded with an electrode outside the cell. They mapped each field with spots, slits and bars. Moving a stimulus and counting spikes shows where the field lies.

scenes.tts: The first class they described was the simple cell. A simple cell has separate ON and OFF subregions, side by side. Light in an ON region excites the cell. Light in an OFF region inhibits it, and removing that light excites it. Light that covered an ON and an OFF region together tended to cancel.
scenes.visual: Field map with an ON strip flanked by OFF strips; a light patch over ON excites, over OFF inhibits, over both cancels (spike ticks).
scenes.narration: The first class they described was the simple cell. A simple cell has separate ON and OFF subregions, side by side. Light in an ON region excites the cell. Light in an OFF region inhibits it, and removing that light excites it. Light that covered an ON and an OFF region together tended to cancel.

scenes.tts: The subregions are elongated, so the orientation of a bar is critical. A bar aligned with the ON strip drove the cell. A bar across the strip barely did. Turn the bar, and the response changes.
scenes.visual: A bar rotates over the ON strip; spike ticks are dense when aligned and nearly absent when across.
scenes.narration: The subregions are elongated, so the orientation of a bar is critical. A bar aligned with the ON strip drove the cell. A bar across the strip barely did. Turn the bar, and the response changes.

scenes.tts: Here is a made-up recording from a V1 cell. The bar sits at the best position, and many trials are averaged. With no bar, the cell fires at two spikes per second. Six orientations draw a tuning curve. The best orientation is ninety degrees, at forty spikes per second. At half height the curve is about sixty-seven degrees wide, an interpolated estimate. The orientation index is zero point nine zero. Near one means a strong preference for the best orientation over the orthogonal one. It does not by itself give the tuning width.
scenes.caption: Here is a made-up recording from a V1 cell. The bar sits at the best position, and many trials are averaged. With no bar, the cell fires at 2 spikes/s. Six orientations draw a tuning curve. The best orientation is 90 degrees, at 40 spikes/s. At half height the curve is about 67 degrees wide, an interpolated estimate. The orientation index is 0.90. scenes.tts: Complex cells keep the orientation preference but tolerate position. A correctly oriented bar drives them over much of the field. No separate ON and OFF regions can be mapped. Hubel and Wiesel suggested that geniculate cells in a row converge on a simple cell, and simple cells converge on a complex cell. That was a proposal, not a demonstration. Keep the rule: in cat visual cortex, bars at the right angle drive cells that spots often miss.
scenes.visual: A bar at several positions drives the complex cell, a rotated bar does not; then LGN boxes to simple to complex with excitatory arrows, tagged proposal.
